title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Quickly get next Sequence/Entry Number (without using FindLast -> Entry No. + 1)
summary: The post explains how to retrieve the next sequence or entry number for ledger tables in Business Central using the Sequence No. Mgt. codeunit instead of the traditional FindLast() + 1 approach. This provides a cleaner, standard pattern for generating primary keys in ledger tables.
key_points: Business Central supports three methods for generating primary keys: No. Series, AutoSplitKey property, and finding the last number then adding 1
Ledger tables use integer Entry No. fields that are automatically incremented, requiring sequence number generation when adding custom data
Codeunit 9500 'Sequence No. Mgt.' provides procedures GetNextSeqNo() and GetCurrentSeqNo() that simplify retrieving sequence numbers without manual FindLast() logic
The sequence codeunit accepts only tables with integer primary keys; non-integer keys will cause runtime errors
Using LockTable() before FindLast() may be necessary to prevent simultaneous insertion conflicts

quotes.text: If the table primary key passed in is not Integer Data Type, a runtime error will occur.
quotes.why_it_matters: Critical constraint that developers must understand to avoid runtime failures when using the codeunit
